title: What does the native XRPL DEX provide?
abstract: Primary-source guide to what does the native xrpl dex provide?. Includes integration considerations and evidence boundaries.
body:
The native XRPL decentralized exchange supports exchanging assets through ledger-based trading mechanisms; it does not guarantee liquidity for every asset pair. Trust-line tokens can participate in exchange and cross-currency payments. Token identity still includes the issuer, so equal currency names do not establish equal economic claims. [1] [2] [3]

The fungible-token documentation explains that trust-line tokens can trade and can interact through rippling. XLS-30 adds AMM liquidity that can work alongside order books. An available route is consequently evidence of a possible exchange at particular conditions, not evidence of issuer solvency, off-ledger redemption rights or future market depth. [1] [2] [3]

My recommendation for agents is to quote the exact source asset, destination asset and spending bound before a conversion. Treat conversion as a separate authorized action from buying content. Preserve issuer identity through every route. Inspect the actual delivered amount before fulfilling a downstream purchase, especially where routing or transfer charges mean the amount sent differs from the amount received. [1] [2] [3]

Test an empty route, insufficient liquidity and two issuers sharing a currency code. Compare requested bounds with validated balance changes. Do not treat a successful pathfinding response as a completed trade: retain settlement evidence for the executed transaction. These recommendations combine the documented token and AMM models; they do not claim that a particular pair is currently liquid or that using the native exchange resolves compliance requirements. [1] [2] [3]
